metadata.sampling: Exact multivariate hypergeometric draws without replacement from released-data cell counts.
metadata.outcome_pairing: Visit and conversion are paired on the same sampled rows, via their joint count cells.
metadata.interpretation: Power and coverage are empirical rejection and coverage rates under repeated sampling without replacement from the full public sample, treated as a finite population whose difference in visit rates is the reference value.
metadata.conversion_interpretation: For secondary conversion analyses, the full public-sample conversion-rate difference is the analogous reference value.
metadata.interval_design: Wald and independent Beta posterior intervals use the ordinary binomial working model without finite-population correction; their empirical finite-population coverage is measured, not assumed.
metadata.analytic_power_assumptions: Two-sided pooled z-test, alpha=0.05, normal approximation at released arm rates. The IID baseline ignores finite-population correction; a second approximation applies it to the alternative variance. Rare-event approximations can be inaccurate.
metadata.mde_assumptions: Two-sided alpha=0.05, 80% target power, local normal approximation at the released control rate, IID baseline without finite-population correction.
metadata.uncertainty: Monte Carlo SE and Wilson intervals quantify replication error; posterior quantiles add numerical simulation error.
metadata.aa_scope: A/A checks the specified test under random splits of the fixed released control pool; it cannot establish randomisation of the original release.

visit.aa_design: The complete control pool is split into complementary random halves in every replication.
visit.test: Two-sided pooled z-test at alpha=0.05 without sequential correction.
visit.peeking_design: Two disjoint cumulative groups from the remaining control pool; 50 correlated looks, 10,000 new users per arm per look.

conversion.aa_design: The complete control pool is split into complementary random halves in every replication.
conversion.test: Two-sided pooled z-test at alpha=0.05 without sequential correction.
conversion.peeking_design: Two disjoint cumulative groups from the remaining control pool; 50 correlated looks, 10,000 new users per arm per look.
